prompt: Explain why a self-judging model drifts while a verifier-checked model compounds.
answer: A self-judging model can drift while a verifier-checked model compounds due to differing mechanisms of model validation and adjustment. Self-judging models rely on internal error metrics to adjust themselves, which can lead to instability or drift as the model relies on these internal checks to continuously improve. This internal self-judging mechanism can cause drift, as the model does not always externalize validation to ensure consistency and correctness (e.g., [sub-question, counter, counter; hop1]). On the other hand, verifier-checked models are validated by external checks, accumulating these consistent validations over time. This method of validation can help compound the adjustments and corrections necessary for the model, leading to a more stable and compound model that is closer to its intended behavior (e.g., [counter, mechanism; hop1, hop2]). The internal self-judging mechanisms of self-judging models and the external validation of verifier-checked models illustrate conflicting approaches where one can lead to model inconsistency or divergence, while the other promotes stability and accuracy.
